- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.33) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for pessimism bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >1.5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and model forecasts are below recent high, model underestimates momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with bullish sentiment.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when price is above 72.00; model tends to overpredict; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0% for 3–5 days post-peak.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and model is flat or slightly rising, model underestimates volatility; add 0.2–0.5% upward bias to capture sentiment-driven noise.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong downward trend, model often fails to recognize reversal; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to avoid premature bearish conclusion.
